testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving through a curve during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your lane if you need to in order to complete the curve.
Slow down after you enter the curve.
Do not look for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Before entering a curve, you must slow down enough so you do not need to brake or shift while in the curve. Keep your vehicle in its lane and watch for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you need to brake?

options.text: Tap your brakes a couple of times.
Stick your arm out the window.
Swerve within your lane.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes a couple of times.
questions.explanation: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down, lightly tap your brake pedal a few times. This makes your brake lights flash.

questions.question: Regrooved tires should not be used where?

options.text: On any vehicle.
On the front wheels of a bus.
On trucks hauling gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front wheels of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, what is your best option to stop?

options.text: An escape ramp.
Drive on the shoulder.
Stay on the road.
Hit a slower vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: An escape ramp.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, use an escape ramp. If there is no escape ramp, look for another escape route, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual air brake system, what should the driver do?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving so fuel reaches the engine.
Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
Begin driving right after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi pressure in both systems. Watch the air pressure gauges to check the pressure.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you block other drivers, what should you do?

options.text: Drive in the left lane.
Use your four-way flashers.
Drive without using any lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive so slowly that you block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to alert drivers behind you (if local laws allow this).

questions.question: When should you check mirror adjustment?

options.text: Once a month.
Before every trip.
Only if you plan to use the mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every trip.
questions.explanation: Check your mirror adjustment before you start every trip. Adjust them as needed.

questions.question: When using a helper to back up a vehicle, where should the helper stand?

options.text: In front of the passenger's side of the vehicle.
In front of the driver's side of the vehicle.
Near the back of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When backing up, use a helper to watch the blind spots. The helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where the driver can see them.

questions.question: Why is traction important?

options.text: For safe braking.
For using turn signals correctly.
For operating the horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: For safe braking.
questions.explanation: You cannot brake or steer your vehicle without good traction. Make sure your tires are in good condition before you drive.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Check traffic first.
Do not use your mirrors.
Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow the instructions.
Do not change lanes if you do not want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic first.
questions.explanation: You will make several lane changes during the driving skills test. Before changing lanes, check traffic and use proper signals. Change lanes smoothly and safely.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians cannot see you. This keeps you safe when passing.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.
Usually notices hazards more slowly.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually notices hazards more slowly.
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers see road dangers more slowly than focused drivers. They may not see dangers at all.

questions.question: Escape ramps are used to:

options.text: Only cars, not trucks.
Leave the highway and enter a two-lane road.
Stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhill roads. They help stop vehicles that lose brake control. They have loose, soft material and sometimes an uphill slope.

questions.question: If spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Push down the brake pedal.
Open the hood.
Release air from the air tanks.
Open the cab door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
A dangerous activity.
Safe if the food is easy to eat.

questions.correctAnswerText: A dangerous activity.
questions.explanation: Eating, smoking, and drinking take your attention off the road. On long trips, plan time to stop and eat safely.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Rarely happens with large trucks.
Usually happens when going faster than 65 mph.
Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. You do not need a lot of water on the road for this to happen.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, once air pressure is lost and spring brakes activate:

options.text: You cannot move the vehicle.
A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use spring brakes to drive normally.
The air tanks will automatically refill to a safe level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a second air tank. You can use it to temporarily release spring brakes if they activate. This lets you move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can let poisonous fumes into the cab.
Does not cause problems.
Is not a concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can let poisonous fumes into the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system allows poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth. Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?

options.text: Drivers speeding
Slow drivers
Animals crossing the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers speeding
questions.explanation: Speeding is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully and slowly near workers.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: Should always come to a complete stop.
May need to swerve out of the way.
Should change lanes without looking.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swerve out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you do not have enough space to stop, swerving may be your safest choice.

questions.question: What happens if a vehicle does not have enough oil in its engine?

options.text: The vehicle will have trouble stopping.
The vehicle will jerk or move in jerky motions while driving.
The engine can be damaged quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be damaged quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine needs enough oil to work properly. If an engine runs without oil, it can be destroyed very quickly.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, what should you check on the hoses?

options.text: For leaks.
To make sure they are clear.
To make sure they are connected to the battery.
To check for the right amount of brake fluid.

questions.correctAnswerText: For leaks.
questions.explanation: When checking a power steering system, look at the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Most importantly, check the hoses for leaks.

questions.question: How much water on the road does it take for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: Usually several inches
A large amount, like a big puddle
Only a small amount
None

questions.correctAnswerText: Only a small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a vehicle's tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. You do not need a lot of water on the road for this to happen.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that looks black because of dirt on the road
Ice that is easy to see

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice may just look wet.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The total weight of a fully loaded vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
The maximum weight a vehicle can tow
The minimum weight a vehicle can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a fully loaded vehicle as stated by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the total weight of a fully loaded vehicle. The manufacturer sets this value.

questions.question: When driving slower than 40 mph, how many seconds of following distance should you keep for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, keep at least one second of distance between you and the vehicle ahead for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At higher speeds, add one more second.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, brake drums should have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.

options.text: One half
One quarter
One third
One tenth

questions.correctAnswerText: One half
questions.explanation: Before driving, check the brake drums during your walk-around inspection. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area width.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being sent to the brakes.
The temperature of the air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being sent to the brakes.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being sent to the brakes. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: When should you NOT use your mirrors?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When making a turn.
To check how fast you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check how fast you are going.
questions.explanation: You should check your mirrors often while driving, especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight movements. Do not use mirrors to check your speed.

questions.question: What is required for over-length loads?

options.text: Special permits.
The road must be closed to other traffic.
A person must walk next to the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Special permits.
questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads may need special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
Not use wheel chocks.
Use wheel chocks only if you have applied the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When parking on a flat surface, always use wheel chocks. This prevents the trailer from rolling if the vehicle does not have spring brakes.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Change a tire.
Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
Estimate the weight of a load on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: You should not use the parking brake:

options.text: If your vehicle is stopped on a level surface.
If your vehicle is stopped on a slight incline.
If your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
If your vehicle's other braking systems seem to be working adequately.

questions.correctAnswerText: If your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if the brakes are very hot from going down a steep hill, or if they are wet in freezing temperatures. Hot brakes can be damaged. Wet brakes in freezing weather can ice up and lock the wheels.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, you should not:

options.text: Ensure that the steering box is securely mounted.
Ensure that the steering box is free of leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Check for power steering fluid leaks and damage to hoses. Do not assume cotter keys are present—verify they are there.

questions.question: Which of the following can help you know when to shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Road speed
Engine speed
Both of the above
None of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: There are two ways to know when to shift up. First, watch engine speed (rpm). Read your vehicle's manual to learn the correct rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second, watch road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, then watch the speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: If you are turning left at an intersection with two available turn lanes:

options.text: It is best to use the right lane.
It doesn't matter which lane you use.
It is best to use the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is best to use the right lane.
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to make a safe left turn. If there are two left turn lanes, always start your turn from the rightmost lane.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually occurs:

options.text: When tires are properly inflated.
When driving at speeds slower than 15 mph.
In areas where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water sits on the road. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water. Under-inflated tires and worn tread increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: The controlled braking method is:

options.text: When the driver locks the wheels and steers.
When the driver applies the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
When the driver only slightly taps the brakes.
When the driver downshifts the gears to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the driver applies the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. If you need to steer while braking, release the brakes, steer, then apply the brakes again.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving skills test, you will be evaluated on your gear usage. You should not:

options.text: Avoid grinding or clashing gears.
Select a gear that does not rev the engine.
Forget to shift through an intersection.
Shift while taking a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift while taking a turn.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, you will be evaluated on gear usage. Select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine. Avoid grinding gears and avoid shifting during turns or intersections.

questions.question: The leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should be no more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.

options.text: 8 psi
5 psi
3 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: 5 psi
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate must not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle should not be driven because it needs repairs.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before starting a trip
While driving
After a trip
Mirrors do not need to be adjusted

questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting a trip
questions.explanation: You must check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Pull the air brake lever
Engage the brake lever
Push the brake pedal down
Pull the brake pedal up

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal down
questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. The harder you push, the more air pressure is released.

questions.question: When driving long distances, you should stop for a break ____ to avoid becoming too tired.

options.text: Every half hour
Every hour
Every two hours
Every six hours

questions.correctAnswerText: Every two hours
questions.explanation: Take a break at least every two hours or every 100 miles to prevent fatigue on long trips.

questions.question: Which of these surfaces is the most slippery?

options.text: Dry ice
Wet ice
Wet pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when it is warm enough to melt ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: How is water and compressor oil removed from an air storage tank?

options.text: The water and oil are siphoned out
A drain valve is opened to remove the water and oil
The water and oil are removed automatically as you use the brakes
A sponge is used to soak up the water and oil

questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve is opened to remove the water and oil
questions.explanation: Open the drain valve to remove water and oil from air storage tanks. If these liquids build up, they can damage the brakes. You must drain manually operated tanks every day.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle
Most trucks cannot go in reverse
Cargo may fall out of the trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Only back up if absolutely necessary.

questions.question: Headlights:

options.text: Are not usually necessary when driving at night
Provide better light than the sun
Should be on high beam whenever possible
Should always be on high beam

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be on high beam whenever possible
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights at night when it is safe and legal. Switch to low beam within 500 feet of approaching vehicles to avoid blinding other drivers.

questions.question: To know if your vehicle can handle a load, you must know:

options.text: The vehicle's suspension rating
The tire rating for the front tires only
The tire rating for the rear tires only

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle's suspension rating
questions.explanation: You are responsible for making sure your vehicle is not overloaded. Know the legal weight limits and your vehicle's weight capacity rating, including the suspension system's rating.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, you must:

options.text: Obtain a hazardous materials endorsement
Drive while using flashing lights
Wear a gas mask

questions.correctAnswerText: Obtain a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials that require vehicle placards.

questions.question: When driving down a long downhill slope, you should brake by:

options.text: Only using the brakes
Mostly using the brakes and sometimes downshifting
Downshifting and then using the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting and then using the brakes
questions.explanation: Before going down a long slope, shift into a lower gear and then brake. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. A lower gear gives you maximum engine braking power to control your speed.
